lessons.story:
At a riverside walking path, Finn reads a map fixed to a board. The map shows north at the top, but the board faces west. Finn assumes that the top of the map means straight ahead from where he stands and starts toward the bicycle parking area.

His sister notices that the bridge should be on their right if they are following the planned route. Instead, it is behind them. They return to the board and compare the north arrow with two visible landmarks: the bridge and a tall red tower.

Once they understand the map's direction, they find the path to the visitor center. It is only a short walk, and they have not needed a new map. The problem came from how Finn connected the drawing to his own position.

Later, Finn sketches a small route for a friend. He marks both a north arrow and the starting point. He also labels the first landmark, giving the reader a way to check the route before walking too far in the wrong direction.
lessons.title: The Map Facing the Wrong Way
